shared_context.content: For integers m >= 2 and h >= 0, K_{m,h} is the set of tuples x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that x_1+...+x_{m-1}=h and, for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i+j < m then x_i+x_j >= x_{i+j}, while if i+j > m then x_i+x_j+1 >= x_{i+j-m}.
shared_context.label: K_definition

shared_context.content: For a positive tuple x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}), let sigma_x be the unique permutation of {1,...,m-1} that orders the pairs (x_i,i) in nondecreasing lexicographic order. Define e_0 = x_{sigma_x(1)} and e_r = x_{sigma_x(r+1)} - x_{sigma_x(r)} for 1 <= r <= m-2. Then x_{sigma_x(k)} = e_0+...+e_{k-1}.
shared_context.label: sorted_difference_encoding

strategy_summary: Partition K_{m,g} into disjoint chambers according to the sorted order of the coordinates, with ties broken by the index. Inside a fixed chamber, encode a tuple by the cumulative differences between consecutive sorted coordinates. The Kunz inequalities then become a finite linear system in these difference variables. Prove a genus-raising injection separately inside each chamber, and then decode and assemble the chamberwise injections into a global injection.
